  • PURPOSE:
    • The purpose of this policy and its supportive guidelines is to ensure safe and appropriate transfer of the patient with minimal risk.
    • The aim is to clarify the clinical accountability of the nursing staff, medical team and supportive staff who are responsible for the patient’s care to ensure that safe, appropriate transfer of patients does occur and their care continues with minimal interruption and risk.
  • SCOPE:

This policy is designed to gauze the requirements of patients who may need to be transferred from wards, departments, Emergency Room, within the Hospital, to diagnostic facilities or to other hospital facilities.

  • RESPONSIBILTY:

CMO, Treating Physician, All Consultants, Staff Nurses trained in ACLS / BLS, staff at Front Office, Casualty, Laboratory and Imaging Services, Ambulance Driver, Security Personnel.

  • ABBREVIATION:
    • AAC: Access, Assessment & Continuity of Care
    • ACLS: Advance Cardiac Life Support
    • BLS: Basic Life Support
    • CCU: Cardiac Care Unit
    • CMO: Chief Medical Officer
    • DAMA: Discharge Against Medical Advice
    • HCO: Health care Organization
    • ICU: Intensive care unit
    • IPD: In Patient Department
    • LAMA: Leaving Against Medical Advice
    • MLC: Medico Legal Case
    • NABH: National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers
    • OPD: Out Patient Department
    • OT: Operation Theatre
  • DEFINITION:
    • Non availability:

Inability to obtain or use appropriate bed for admission of patient to suite his / her needs

    • Referral-out of patient:

Safe transfer of a patient to another organization due to non- availability of required resources including expert / equipment / facility

    • Stable Patient:

Describes physical & mental health condition of a patient which is fixed and not likely to change. In addition patient has normal neurological cardiovascular and respiratory variable and he is in a state of good compensation.

    • Unstable patient:

A patient whose vital parameters need external assistance for their maintenance.

An unstable patient is one who has suffered sudden and extreme deterioration in his physical, mental or emotional well being, leading to a threat to his life. Such a patient may suffer from a coma with a Glasgow coma scale of <10/15, persistent seizures, severe alterations in cardiovascular or respiratory variables leading to de-compensation.

  • REFERENCE:
    • NABH Standards for Hospitals
    • There is an appropriate mechanism for transfer (in and out) or referral of patients.
  • POLICY:
    • Intra-hospital:
      • Patients being transferred within the hospital from one unit to the other i.e. ward to OT should be accompanied by a nursing staff of the ward along with the medical record and all investigation reports, medicines etc. to the receiving unit and handover the patient to the nurse in charge..
      • In the case of an unstable patient, a doctor also accompanies the patient during the transfer.
    • Inter Hospital
      • In the event of the patient being transported for any reason to another facility for investigations, treatment or any other purpose identified hospital personnel should accompany the patient in the ambulance and handover the patient along with all the records and a copy of the summary of treatment given to the nurse of the hospital where the patient is transferred to.
      • However in the situation of an unstable patient being transferred to another facility thus he / she should be transported in an ALS ambulance after cross-checking all the equipment and drugs and accompanied by a medical officer and a Nurse.
  • PROCEDURE:
    • Transfer-in of patients
      • Planned transfer:
        • Information is taken from the organization sending patient to our hospital
        • For unstable / suspected unstable patient; trained person with equipped ambulance is sent & bed is reserved as per need.
      • Unplanned transfer:
        • Patient is accepted only if our hospital can provide service & bed is available.
        • Or else patient is stabilized and referred to other center for further management after verifying that the referred center can provide required service.
    • Referral of patient to other center
      • Indications:
        • If there is no possibility of bed availability
        • If the patient is not agreeable to be admitted in another class
        • Service not available
        • Patient’s choice
      • The treating doctor is asked to possibly defer the admission of the patient or refer the patient to another center.
      • In case of transfer of patients in a life threatening situation (like those who are on ventilator) to another organization, a doctor / ACLS Trained Staffs accompanies the patient. The ambulance driver helper, nurse (Trained in BLS and / or ACLS) or doctor accompany during transfer for unstable Patients to other organizations
      • Decision for transfer to other facility shall be taken by consultant with consent of patient & relatives and same shall be noted on OPD / IPD / Emergency case-paper.
      • In case of emergency, the concerned consultant is informed by the Medical Officer on duty. Consultant’s advice is taken before transferring the patient.
      • Oral and written consent of the patient is taken on the case paper.
      • In case of unknown patients police is informed.
      • Treatment given and diagnosis is written on the case paper.
      • Driver is informed to keep the ambulance ready.
      • Referral slip is given to the patient / relative.
      • In case of unstable patient a call is made in the concerned department at referring Hospital or any other hospital of patient’s choice.
      • The receiving hospital’s decision will be taken orally or written.
      • If the patient’s condition is unstable, he should be stabilized in emergency before transferring.
      • If the patient is serious (as decided by doctor), an ambulance with critical care facility shall be arranged.
      • Patient shall deposit the ambulance charge to the Office In-Charge at the destination and collect the receipt for the same.
    • Transfer / referral of unstable patients:
      • List of Unstable Patients:
        • Glasgow coma scale < 14.
        • Pulse < 60 or > 120 beats per minute.
        • Systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg after a crystalloid fluid challenge of 2 liters.
        • Systolic blood pressure > 190 mm Hg.
        • Respiratory rate < 12 or > 24 breaths per minute.
        • Poor gas exchange, with oxygen saturation < 90%.
        • Temperature < 92°F (< 33°C).
        • Paralysis.
        • Hoarseness or inability to talk.
        • Labored respirations.
        • Severe pain.
        • External hemorrhage.
        • Combative.
        • Severe deformity involving spine, neck, chest or extremities.
        • Penetrating wound from head to popliteal fossa.
      • Requests from other health care providers to transfer patients who have an emergency medical condition and require emergency and tertiary level medical care not available at that facility should be immediately approved when services, space, facilities, and personnel are available to provide appropriate care.
      • When the facility making the transfer request is capable of providing the necessary care, that facility must stabilize the emergency medical condition prior to transfer.
      • When the transferring facility is requesting the transfer of an unstable patient, the following conditions must be met:
        • Physician certification that the expected benefits of transfer outweigh the risks of transfer
        • Patient or family consent when possible
        • Attempts made by the transferring hospital, within its capability, to stabilize the patient in order to minimize any risks of the individual during transfer
        • Our capacity and capability to treat the transferred patient
        • Delivery of all appropriate medical records
        • Transfer shall be made with qualified personnel and transportation equipment.
      • If an emergency patient requires services not available at our hospital, the transfer shall be refused with a recommendation to contact another facility with the necessary capability.
      • The hospital staff member shall obtain the details of the patients’ emergent medical condition and contact Admitting Desk. Admitting Desk shall verify that beds are available.
      • All departments who receive requests for transfer of patients shall maintain this policy and procedure statement in a place accessible to medical staff, and other personnel to ensure that physicians who are involved in transfers adhere to its content. Questions shall be referred to consultant.
      • Similarly, when resources matching the patient needs are not available at our hospital patients shall be transferred other hospital that can meet the patient’s needs.
      • The Consultant / Residential Medical Officer shall contact the faculty of the receiving hospital to ensure that eligibility guidelines are met. Transportation arrangements and a medical escort (if needed) shall be made through the Residential Medical Officer.
      • Patients being transferred from our hospital shall be accompanied by a transfer summary that shall include details of the patient medical condition, interventions done and the ongoing needs of the patient.
      • Stabilization prior to transfer shall include securing the airway (if needed), intravenous access, appropriate fluid replacement and pain control.
    • Transfer / referral of stable patients:
      • It is the policy of our hospital to accept the transfer of stable, non-emergent patients when space, facilities, and personnel are available.
      • Every effort shall be made to accept patients when the sending facility does not have the space, facilities or personnel to provide safe and appropriate care.
      • Transfers of stable, non-emergent patients to higher referral center may be made by contacting a Consultant physician of the Hospital.
      • Stable, non-emergent transfers shall be directly admitted to hospital units.
      • Transportation arrangements for patients to be transferred from our hospital shall be made through the Casualty Medical Officer.
      • Similarly, when resources matching the patient needs are not available at our hospital, patients shall be transferred to facilities that can meet the patient’s needs. Appropriate transportation arrangements and a medical escort (if needed) shall be made through the Casualty Medical Officer.
    • Staff responsible for transfer:
      • Hospital has designated staff responsible during transfer intra / inter hospital
      • Treating consultant decides whom to send after examining the patient.

    • Documentation:
      • Transfer Summary:
        • For transfers / referrals; transfer summary is issued which includes significant findings & treatment given.
        • SBAR transfer form is used for this purpose.
        • For inter hospital transfer; transfer summary is issued.
      • Discharge Summary:
        • For discharges, discharge summary is issued.
        • Same procedure is followed for DAMA too.
        • A copy of discharge summary is retained by the hospital.
